questions.prompt: Create an annotated heatmap from an already-computed correlation matrix.

content.template:
# corr is a DataFrame:
# rows/columns = numeric feature names
# values = correlation coefficients from -1 to 1
#
# Goal: color-coded matrix with the numeric values written in each cell.

sns.{{plot_func}}(corr, {{annotation}}=True)

questions.explanation: `sns.heatmap` maps matrix values to cell colors. `annot=True` writes the values inside the cells, which is useful when the matrix is small enough to read. A scatter plot does not preserve the row/column matrix structure.

questions.prompt: Compute correlations only for numeric DataFrame columns, then plot an annotated heatmap.

content.template:
# df columns:
# age: int
# income: float
# rating: float
# segment: string
#
# Only the numeric columns belong in the correlation matrix.

corr = df.{{corr_method}}(numeric_only={{numeric}})
sns.{{plot_func}}(corr, annot=True)

questions.explanation: `df.corr(numeric_only=True)` creates the square numeric correlation matrix; the string `segment` column is excluded. `sns.heatmap(..., annot=True)` then visualizes that matrix and writes each coefficient in its cell.

# segment: string
#

# color = segment

    data=df,
    vars=["age", "income", "rating"],
    {{semantic}}="segment",
)

questions.explanation: `sns.pairplot` builds a figure-level matrix of pairwise relationships for the selected numeric variables. `hue="segment"` colors observations by segment across the grid. This differs from `scatterplot`, which draws only one x/y relationship on one Axes.

questions.prompt: Order the steps for plotting average monthly revenue by region after starting from transaction-level rows.

items.label: Ensure month is represented as an ordered datetime/month value
Compute average revenue for each month-region group
Use a line plot with month on x, average revenue on y, and region as hue

questions.explanation: The time field must be usable in the intended order before aggregation. Then the transaction rows are grouped and summarized, and the resulting table is passed to the plotting function. Plotting before the aggregation would visualize raw transaction rows rather than the requested monthly averages.
